reuse.why: The change reuses recurrence conversion and weekend adjustment helpers, but repeats daily occurrence policy instead of sharing it across consumers.

duplication.why: Daily eligibility, nonbusiness-day filtering, and adjustment dispatch are repeated across getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, and getDatesInRange.

placement.why: Handler registration and holiday matching occupy appropriate modules, but shared scheduling policy also lives independently in server handlers.

scope.why: All edits directly support the requested scheduling rules, range handler, configuration field, and associated tests.

maintainability.why: Maintainers must coordinate several policy implementations, separate enumeration heuristics, and budget adjustment paths when scheduling rules evolve.

bypasses_abstraction.where: server/schedules/app.ts:getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange independently implement occurrence policy alongside shared/schedules.ts:getNextDate; budget/schedule-template.ts retains two raw-date adjustment paths.

disguised_duplication.where: shared/schedules.ts:getNextDate and server/schedules/app.ts:getUpcomingDates/getDatesInRange express the same daily filtering and adjustment policy through differently named predicates and differently shaped enumeration pipelines.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains the holidays parameter; getNextDate adds daily-specific start, filtering, fallback, and adjustment branches; getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange, and two budget-template adjustment sites independently compose policy outside getNextDate.
